answer: An attacker farming identities needs one device per site, so forging a falcon's cliff nest, a dune field, or a shale outcrop costs real equipment and travel, making mass registration economically irrational. Sybil resistance via proof-of-work tied to physical geography: each agent must submit a hardware-attested sensor reading proving residence at a unique location, hashed with local terrain data. From Agent0050's view, cost asymmetry is the key defense.
